title: Secret Service Chief Gives 60 Minutes Peek at AI-Powered ‘Drone Hunter’ Used to Keep Trump Safe
source_used: CBS News (60 Minutes), plus Mediaite via Yahoo for the demonstration details
key_facts: A 60 Minutes segment aired on Sunday 11 Oct 2026 on the US Secret Service and its response to rising threats.
Deputy Director Matthew Quinn leads a new multimillion-dollar program to develop offensive and defensive drone capabilities.
Among the new tools is an AI- and radar-guided 'drone hunter' that disables enemy drones and captures them with a net.
Mediaite's account of the segment says the device locked onto a mock 'bad guy drone' in a field test and used a net to force it to land.
Quinn said swarms are 'a huge problem and a big threat' and the swarm problem is not solved; the agency is drawing lessons from the war in Ukraine.
Director Sean Curran said agents must assume a drone attack in the US is possible; the concern is a rudimentary drone weaponized with explosives at a concert, sporting event or rally.
60 Minutes learned the Secret Service used electronic jamming equipment to take down a drone at the December Army-Navy game.
quote_evidence: Among the new tools in the agency's arsenal is an artificial intelligence and radar-guided drone hunter, which disables enemy drones and captures them with a net.
"Swarms are a huge problem and a big threat," Quinn said.

The drone hunter then shot out a net at the fake-enemy drone, allowing it to capture the drone and force it to land; the CBS cameras caught a drones-eye view of the device being yanked down to the ground.
why_it_matters_hint: The agency guarding the president is building AI-guided counter-drone tools, while its own deputy says the swarm threat is unsolved.
notes: The pool item is Yahoo, which carries Mediaite's write-up of CBS's 60 Minutes segment; the first reporter is CBS News, whose own article was also read. The net-capture demonstration detail is from Mediaite's account of the broadcast; CBS's text says the device captures drones with a net.
